title: Claudius Conquers Britain
objective: After this level you can describe Claudius's reign and the invasion of Britain.
summary: The guard made Claudius emperor in 41 CE. The scholar few took seriously invaded Britain in 43 CE, where Boudica later rose in revolt.

cards.headline: The emperor nobody took seriously conquered a land Caesar only raided.
The unlikely emperor
cards.body: After Caligula’s murder, the Praetorian Guard made his uncle Claudius emperor in 41 CE. Claudius had a limp and a stammer, and his family kept him out of public life. He was a scholar who wrote histories, now lost, and he relied on freedmen, formerly enslaved people, as powerful officials.

cards.headline: Britain becomes Roman
cards.body: In 43 CE Claudius launched the invasion of Britain, which became a Roman province. In about 60 CE Boudica, queen of the Iceni, led a revolt that burned London before the Romans crushed it.

cards.fact: Caesar had raided Britain twice, in 55 and 54 BCE.
cards.context: Claudius’ invasion came nearly a century later, and this time Rome stayed.

cards.headline: Britain: conquered
learned: The guard made Claudius emperor in 41 CE
He was a scholar kept out of public life

questions.prompt: When did Claudius launch the invasion of Britain?
questions.explanation: Claudius invaded Britain in 43 CE, and it became a province.

questions.prompt: Why was Claudius an unexpected emperor?

options.label: His family had kept him out of public life
He had never been to Rome before
options.rationale: He grew up in the imperial family.

options.label: He was born a Gaulish prince
He had led a revolt against Caligula
options.rationale: The guard chose him after the murder.

questions.explanation: With a limp and a stammer, Claudius was kept out of public life until the guard made him emperor.

questions.prompt: From Level 38: what had Julius Caesar achieved in Britain?

options.label: Full conquest of the whole island

questions.explanation: Caesar led two expeditions to Britain but did not conquer it.
